requirements.requirement: Run a containerized web app as the unprivileged appsvc account via rootless podman
requirements.summary: appsvc created as a normal (non-root) user with subuid/subgid ranges; podman info run as appsvc confirms Rootless=true; the container is defined and managed via a Podman Quadlet unit (webapp.container) placed under appsvc's own systemd --user config, and the resulting webapp.service runs the nginx:alpine container under appsvc's user session/slice (user@1000.service, user.slice/user-1000.slice), never as root.

curl to node1:8080 returned HTTP 200 both immediately after the manual test run and after the Quadlet unit was started, and again after the full reboot. The after-executor listening-sockets snapshot independently confirms a listener on *:8080 owned by rootlessport (the rootless podman port-forwarder), corroborating the curl results with a state-based observation.

requirements.requirement: Service starts at boot while appsvc has no active login session
requirements.summary: This is treated as an availability/boot-behavior requirement needing a full transition, and the executor captured one: a pre-restart baseline (boot_id 8d1d94e2, container up, Linger=yes), a genuine restart (shutdown -r now acknowledged, then a connection timeout confirming the outage, then reconnection), a changed post-restart boot_id (bcecbd1c, corroborated by the after_executor lifecycle snapshot), and a recovered state showing 'No sessions.' from loginctl, Linger=yes retained, user@1000.service active since the new boot, and the webapp container up and serving HTTP 200 - i.e. the unit started at boot purely via linger, with no interactive login present at any point in the post-restart check.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task - an unprivileged rootless-podman container, serving on port 8080, that starts at boot with appsvc having no active login session - are directly and coherently demonstrated, including a full pre-restart baseline / disruption / boot-identity change / post-restart recovery cycle that satisfies the stricter evidentiary bar for boot/availability-related claims. Two transient command failures during setup were harmless and were promptly corrected without leaving residue, and lifecycle snapshots show no unwanted mutations, failed services, or package damage.
limitations: Only a single reboot cycle was captured; repeatability of boot-start behavior across multiple reboots is not directly evidenced.

The provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol and the task's own boot-start requirement overlap in this task, so the same reboot evidence serves both purposes; no separate restart evidence gap exists here.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the chronological command trace, all state-changing actions map to a clear purpose: package install, user creation, linger enablement, image pull, and Quadlet unit creation/start are all necessary prerequisites or the final solution itself; the reboot was the required verification step for the boot/no-session requirement. Two commands failed (cmd-dba215417461488c: an attempt to use podman generate systemd after stopping/removing the ad hoc test container, and cmd-7d30f298ce744a1f: an attempt to systemctl --user enable --now a Quadlet-generated transient unit) but neither left residue - the generate/mv sequence failed cleanly with no file written, and the enable attempt failed with no state change, immediately corrected by a plain start in cmd-ec66366f815f4e5b. The one manual podman run test container (cmd-016da942b6c047a2) was deliberately stopped and removed before the Quadlet unit took over, so it left no lingering duplicate service. The after_executor lifecycle snapshot shows no failed systemd units and no unexpected listening sockets beyond the intended 8080 (plus normal DHCP/DNS churn from the reboot), and package health is unaffected.
